Thought leadership

Protecting Children in the Age of AI — Live on Maalaimurasu

On Instagram's end-to-end encryption rollback, 11 child-safety laws across India, the EU, UK, and US, and what every AI/tech leader owes the next generation.

Watch on YouTube ↗
Read the full reflection ↓

This is a long post — but I believe it's one of the most important things I've written. Please read till the end.

This morning, I spoke live on Maalaimurasu about Instagram removing End-to-End Encryption from May 8, 2026.

But the conversation left me thinking much deeper than just one platform's decision.

When I work on AI, I carry a responsibility that goes far beyond the product I build.

Behind every algorithm is a child scrolling at midnight.
Behind every data point is a family that trusts us.
Behind every feature decision is a society that doesn't always get a vote.

We talked about 11 laws across India, EU, UK and USA — all trying to answer one question: how do we protect children in a digital world that moves faster than regulation?

IT Act. DPDP Rules. EU Chat Control. UK Online Safety Act. EARN IT Act.

Governments are trying. Tech companies are navigating. And somewhere in between — a 14-year-old is on Instagram not knowing what "end-to-end encryption" means, or why it matters.

That gap — between what policymakers write and what a child understands — is exactly where leaders like us must show up.

Not just as technologists. But as educators. As parents. As coaches.

Three things I believe every AI/tech leader must do:

  1. Teach the next generation — peers, subordinates, your own kids — what digital privacy means in plain language. Not jargon. Real talk.
  2. Build with intention — every AI feature you ship asks: does this protect or expose the most vulnerable?
  3. Pass it on — the knowledge you carry about data, privacy, AI safety shouldn't stay in boardrooms. It belongs in classrooms, dinner tables, and WhatsApp family groups.

AI is not neutral. It reflects the values of the people who build it.

What values are we passing on?

Honestly, this appearance was less about me sharing expertise — and more a session that made me think. Deeply. About my role, my responsibility, and what I owe to the next generation.

05 — Case Study

AI-Built Compliance Training — From Regulation to Certified Workforce

A repeatable approach to turning any regulated process — document verification, safety compliance, financial KYC, healthcare credentialing — into bilingual, interactive e-learning, built end-to-end with AI and shipped in weeks, not quarters.

9 weeks, kickoff to launch ~10,000 learners in the example deployment 2+ languages supported 4 modules + certification quiz SCORM · Any LMS

Frontline and regulated workforces everywhere need to learn a detailed verification or compliance process before they're allowed to transact — checking documents, inspecting equipment, following a mandated workflow. Building that training usually takes months: subject-matter experts write it, a vendor builds it, legal reviews it, and by the time it ships, the requirement has often already changed.

This platform is built to close that gap: a document-centered layout, a word-level teleprompter synced to audio, a language switch, dark mode, and full play/pause/resume — coded end-to-end in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then packaged as SCORM so it drops into any LMS. The knowledge base is authored with Claude and iterated against real compliance requirements until sign-off, using fictional sample documents so it can train on realistic detail without ever touching real user data. Process walkthroughs are screen-recorded and edited in DaVinci Resolve — the same pipeline reusable for the next regulated workflow, not rebuilt from scratch each time.

06 — Case Study

AI-Powered Customer Service Transformation

A programme that replaces manual contact-centre handling with self-service voice, chat, and email — deployed language by language across a global, multi-market operation, without breaking compliance, payment rails, or brand voice along the way.

18 countries in scope ~559,000 monthly contacts 8 languages, phased rollout 34+ APIs integrated

Enterprise contact centres handling hundreds of thousands of contacts a month usually run on manual agent workflows and basic keypad IVR — expensive to scale, inconsistent across languages, and slow to change. Standing up real conversational AI across voice, chat, and email at that volume means integrating identity verification, account systems, and payment rails without breaking compliance or brand voice, market by market.

This platform replaces manual handling with self-service journeys: identity verification — document and PIN checks, with voice biometrics layered in for fraud mitigation — account self-service, registration and plan changes, PCI-compliant payments, and a knowledge base spanning dozens of FAQ categories across every market, rolled out language by language and prioritized by volume and business criticality. Behind the scenes, an intent-routing agent classifies what the customer needs and hands the conversation to the right specialist: a deterministic agent for rule-bound flows like identity checks and payments, an LLM-powered agent for open-ended or ambiguous requests, and a dedicated QnA agent that answers straight from the knowledge base. APIs are scoped and exposed for every business scenario, prompts are tuned line by line to match brand voice, and a rapid-prototyping track runs in parallel with design so the business can react to real conversations before build even starts.

Before committing to the build, the competitive landscape gets benchmarked directly — interacting with rival customer-service channels across multiple markets. In practice, most are still running basic keypad IVR with no conversational AI at all, and the few with natural-language bots still fall back to menus or push straight to an agent. That gap sets the bar for what "ahead of the market" needs to mean.

07 — Case Study

Catastrophe Risk Analytics for Underwriting

A geospatial risk-analysis product that turns raw hazard data into a defensible view of what a hurricane — or any catastrophic peril — would do to a specific book of business, built to survive both a modeling review and a sales call.

Hurricane, wind & flood perils modeled Python & R analytics stack Shapefile-based geospatial overlays Portfolio-level exposure scoring

Insurers and reinsurers need to know how a catastrophic event will actually affect their own book of business — not just a generic hazard map. Off-the-shelf storm and flood data doesn't map cleanly onto a company's real portfolio of policies, and without that translation, underwriters and executives can't act on it with confidence.

This product closes that gap with a full analytics pipeline: exploratory data analysis to understand the shape and quality of the underlying hazard and exposure data, statistical models fit to historical loss and hazard history to predict impact severity, and a geospatial layer — built with shapefiles in Python and R — that overlays hurricane tracks, wind fields, and flood zones directly onto a client's actual property portfolio. The output is a visualization a risk officer can read directly: which policies sit in the projected path, how exposed they are, and what that means in dollars.

The same models and visualizations also became a pre-sales tool: instead of pitching the product's capability in the abstract, a client's own book of business gets run through the pipeline live, showing exactly what a specific hurricane scenario would do to their actual portfolio — a far more convincing argument than a features list.
